## 1. Open Studio on the Agents pillar

The Agents pillar lists every agent forge can dispatch.

![Open Studio on the Agents pillar](/media/stories/S5/01-open-studio-on-the-agents-pillar.png)

## 2. Press "+ New agent"

A new agent starts from a starter — a ready-made shape the operator edits — or from nothing at all.

![Press "+ New agent"](/media/stories/S5/02-press-new-agent.png)

## 3. Start from the Blank agent starter, name it "story S5", and say what it exists to do

Every agent needs one sentence that says why it exists, because that sentence is what a planner reads when it decides which agent to put at a station.

![Start from the Blank agent starter, name it "story S5", and say what it exists to do](/media/stories/S5/03-start-from-the-blank-agent-starter-name-.png)

## 4. Write the instructions: what this agent does, step by step

The purpose says why this agent exists; the instructions say how it works, and forge hands that body to the agent as its brief at dispatch time.

![Write the instructions: what this agent does, step by step](/media/stories/S5/04-write-the-instructions-what-this-agent-d.png)

## 5. Open Advanced and compose the two skills this agent needs

Composing is the whole idea: an agent is not written, it is assembled out of skills the library already holds.

![Open Advanced and compose the two skills this agent needs](/media/stories/S5/05-open-advanced-and-compose-the-two-skills.png)

## 6. Set the tool fence: this agent may invoke git and Node, and nothing else

The fence is the point of the Advanced drawer.

![Set the tool fence: this agent may invoke git and Node, and nothing else](/media/stories/S5/06-set-the-tool-fence-this-agent-may-invoke.png)

## 7. Leave the MCP zone empty — the fence is a closed list, not a starting point

This agent talks to a repo and a browser.

![Leave the MCP zone empty — the fence is a closed list, not a starting point](/media/stories/S5/07-leave-the-mcp-zone-empty-the-fence-is-a-.png)

## 8. Save the agent

Saving mints the agent and lands the operator on its own page.

![Save the agent](/media/stories/S5/08-save-the-agent.png)

## 9. Check the agent is ready — every readiness check the panel names

Readiness is forge refusing to pretend.

![Check the agent is ready — every readiness check the panel names](/media/stories/S5/09-check-the-agent-is-ready-every-readiness.png)

## 10. Cap what this run may spend at $2

A real agent costs real money, so the operator sets the cap before starting the run rather than discovering the bill afterwards — and the button says the figure back to them.

![Cap what this run may spend at $2](/media/stories/S5/10-cap-what-this-run-may-spend-at-2.png)

## 11. Run the agent standalone against the story's own project

Standalone is an agent off the graph: no Flow, no station, just this agent against this project because the operator asked.

![Run the agent standalone against the story's own project](/media/stories/S5/11-run-the-agent-standalone-against-the-sto.png)

## 12. Watch the run land in the agent’s own history

Every dispatch this agent has ever had is on its own page.

![Watch the run land in the agent’s own history](/media/stories/S5/12-watch-the-run-land-in-the-agent-s-own-hi.png)

## 13. Read the row: what it cost, where it ran, and how it ended

This is where S5 ends, and the word that matters is honest.

![Read the row: what it cost, where it ran, and how it ended](/media/stories/S5/13-read-the-row-what-it-cost-where-it-ran-a.png)
